question: Should OpenClaw replace its documented one-user trusted-operator gateway model with an opt-in shared-gateway member boundary, and should core permanently own the associated identity, RBAC, device-trust, storage, protocol, and Plugin SDK contracts?
rationale: Implementation review cannot decide a deliberate change to the project’s published threat model and permanent public contracts without explicit repository and security-owner intent.

options.title: Keep the current trust model
options.body: Do not merge the core multi-user boundary; retain per-user gateway isolation and use external deployment layers where adequate.

options.title: Sponsor a core Teams boundary
options.body: Approve the direction with named gateway, Plugin SDK, Workspaces, and secops ownership, then require a threat-model update and staged proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to generic extension seams
options.body: Retain only independently useful generic resource APIs and defer accounts, sessions, pairing, and the portal until a separate product decision.

recommendation.title: Keep the current trust model
recommendation.body: Do not merge the core multi-user boundary; retain per-user gateway isolation and use external deployment layers where adequate.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest product-routing candidate from the merged Workspaces history and repository ownership, with openclaw/openclaw-secops required for the security decision.
